summary: @servicetitan/eslint-config preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes an obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package's `preinstall` script runs `node setup.mjs`, which is itself variable-name-obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style hex identifiers wrapping `fs`, `https`, `zlib`, and string-constant maps for `--version`, `ldd`, `musl`, `/etc/os-release`, `Alpine`). setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime (pinned v1.3.13) from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/...` into a tmp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it with `execFileSync(bunPath, [path.join(D, 'math_init.js')])`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB `@bun @bun-cjs` compiled bundle heavily obfuscated with string-array rotation (`WV8StW` shifter, large mixed-literal `n7gIxM` array, base64-alphabet decoder `hc1jfK9`); its purpose is undocumented. An ESLint configuration package has no legitimate need to fetch a second language runtime at install time and hand it an opaque bundled payload; the composed pattern (obfuscated loader + alternate-runtime fetch + opaque obfuscated payload executed on `npm install`) matches the alternate-runtime dropper shape.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
